Pre-fix controller at f22b9dff59454391a50a255a39995bf635deea9e^ = 534841df7efff24065f17c9debb6d91c24430b61:concrete/controllers/single_page/dashboard/extend/update.php do_update($pkgHandle) checks only canInstallPackages(), then packageController->testForUpgrade()/upgradeCoreData()/upgrade() with no token->validate and no HTTP method guard.

Tag 9.5.0 c747e425266ac50c12b5f2f74fa895ecec5cd777 view concrete/single_pages/dashboard/extend/update.php invokes do_update via $ch->button(..., View::url('/dashboard/extend/update', 'do_update', $pkg->getPackageHandle())), i.e. a state-changing GET navigation.

Fix f22b9dff59454391a50a255a39995bf635deea9e requires POST and $this->token->validate('update_addon') before the same upgrade sink; 9.5.1 view switches the button to a POST form emitting $valt->output('update_addon').

Source-to-sink: attacker GET /dashboard/extend/update/do_update/<pkgHandle> in an admin session that passes canInstallPackages() with the named package already installed -> upgradeCoreData()/upgrade() as the web server user.

Smallest surviving public first-write of the CSRF-less package-upgrade action is 6ac5687f09b766158e43932ebbf5367d5e787792 (Andrew Embler, 2009-08-13, git-svn-id svn.concrete5.org r1196) adding public function update($pkgHandle) { ... $p->upgradeCoreData(); $p->upgrade(); } to trunk/web/concrete/controllers/dashboard/install.php with no token check.
Parent already used validation/token on sibling uninstall_* methods, so the omission is specific to the new update() action rather than a missing CSRF helper.
